flags.name: F029-2
flags.issue: Version numbers clash when several pull requests are open: each build takes "the next free number" at its last sync, so two open builds take the same one (028 and 029 both took v3.19.00) and whichever merges second must sync again. The checks only require a higher build and a different version, so…
flags.issueFull: Version numbers clash when several pull requests are open: each build takes "the next free number" at its last sync, so two open builds take the same one (028 and 029 both took v3.19.00) and whichever merges second must sync again. The checks only require a higher build and a different version, so skipping or merging out of order isn't caught either
flags.next: Recommended: the status board reserves numbers in the order pull requests are marked Ready (it already lists each build's number under VERSION and can show a clash), each build takes its reserved number, and the Editor merges in that order. A sync is then needed only when the order changes. Alternative (no clashes at all, but more machinery): a workflow writes the version and build onto main after each merge. Needs a CLAUDE.md change by the design chat

flags.issueFull: Bot minimum: at 5v5, Arrow Storm warm-ups that end unfired rise from 0 (v3.9) to 88 in 1,000 games (7.4% of 1,190 warm-ups), above the brief's "more than half" line. Example: seed XRWD-ALC9-SXS5 (v310-5v5, North first), South's Light Ranged warms up at E6 on turn 6 and lapses on turn 7. At 7v7 they barely move (308 to 332 lapsed). Storm is still worth warming: it deals 10.7 a firing at 5v5 and 10.5 at 7v7 against a normal hit of about 5.6, though it kills on 4% of firings at 5v5 (85% on v3.9) and 45% at 7v7 (80%)

flags.name: F028-2
flags.issue: 5v5 now favours the second mover. storm-v310 (Brain 8 mirrors, 1,000 games per format, same seeds as v3.9): the first mover's share of decisive 5v5 games falls from 53.5% (v3.9) to 41.9% on v3.10 (766 decisive games; about 4.5 standard errors below even and 3 points under F12's 45% floor). 7v7…
flags.issueFull: 5v5 now favours the second mover. storm-v310 (Brain 8 mirrors, 1,000 games per format, same seeds as v3.9): the first mover's share of decisive 5v5 games falls from 53.5% (v3.9) to 41.9% on v3.10 (766 decisive games; about 4.5 standard errors below even and 3 points under F12's 45% floor). 7v7 moves into range: 44.6% to 49.2%. FD49-3's 56.5% for 5v5 was measured at Command 8 (first turn 5); v3.10's 5v5 plays the preset's Command 10, first turn 6, so that prediction never applied to this rule set. That Command is the cause is likely, not isolated. Fighting also starts much earlier at 5v5 (first attack turn 4.3 to 1.3; turn-limit games 44.3% to 23.4%), likely because Brain 8 no longer holds back from a Storm that can't one-shot its archer
flags.next: Recommended: keep v3.10 as built (the Editor's ruling) and measure 5v5 Command (8 or 10, first turn equal against reduced) in the Cavalry build's Command comparison, as F022-9 plans. If 5v5 matters before then, a sim-only screen of 5v5 at first-turn Command 8 and 10 on v3.10 answers it in a day. 27 Nov: the Editor asked about equal Command; screen command-v310-screen queued (200 games each: 7v7 and 5v5 at Command 10 with first turn 6 and 10; 5v5 at Command 8 with first turn 5 and 8). Promising settings go to a 1,000-game confirm overnight 27 Nov result (results/v3.19.00/2026-11-27_screen_command-v310-screen/, 200 games each, same seeds): 7v7 first turn 6 gives 47.9%, equal first turn 10 gives 67.3% (about 5 standard errors apart): equal Command at 7v7 hands the first mover the game, so keep 6. 5v5: the first-turn number changes nothing. Brain 8's first mover never spends more than 5 Command on its first turn at 5v5 (average 4.2), so a cap of 5, 6, 8 or 10 never binds and every pair played identical games (33.3% at Command 10, 57.4% at Command 8). Command 8 nears even but turn-limit games rise from 23.5% to 39.0%. Whether the 5-Command ceiling is the rules or Brain 8 is likely the bot, not isolated. No setting earns an overnight confirm; see F028-4

flags.issueFull: When a new push to a pull request cancels its lab run mid-play (Brief 024's cancel-in-progress), the "merge and file the results" step still ran: it filed an empty run (0 games, "Failed: ... cancelled") into results/, committed it to the pull request and moved the job order to studies/done/, so the next push played nothing. Seen on PR #65 (storm-v310). Brief 028 removed the empty folder and moved the order back to the queue by hand
flags.next: Recommended: a later lab brief makes the merge step skip filing (and leave the order queued) when every play part was cancelled. Until then, a build with a job order should not push while its lab run is playing

flags.issueFull: F022-7 happened again on PR 60: a docs-only push (the Report) started a new lab run, which cancelled the one playing the three screens after 70 minutes. The cancelled run filed 30% of the games (6 of 20 parts) and moved all three job orders to studies/done/. The lab's paths filter doesn't protect a pull request: GitHub checks it against everything the pull request changes, so every push to a pull request with a job order or a version change restarts the lab. Code re-queued the orders (the partial run folders stay as filed, marked Failed) and pushes nothing more until they finish
flags.next: Recommended: the lab fix brief F022-7 asks for also skips the cancel when the new push changes nothing under studies/queue/, board/ or sims/lab/
